name: Singshore Bridge
tagline: Sikkim's highest bridge, 240 m across a gorge near Uttarey
meta_description: Singshore Bridge: a 240 m suspension bridge over 100 m above a gorge between Dentam and Uttarey, West Sikkim. How to reach from Pelling, costs and tips.
summary: Singshore Bridge is a suspension bridge about 240 m long and more than 100 m above a forested gorge, on the road between Dentam and Uttarey in Gyalshing district (West Sikkim). Wikipedia calls it the highest bridge in Sikkim. It is about 26 km and 1–1.5 hours from Pelling. Allow 30–60 minutes.
intro: The road west from Pelling drops into the Dentam valley and then climbs towards Uttarey. Partway up, it crosses a deep, forested gorge on the Singshore Bridge, a single long span of steel and concrete that Wikipedia describes as about 240 m long and more than 100 m high, the highest bridge in Sikkim. The district administration repeats a common claim that it is the second highest bridge in Asia; we cannot verify the ranking, but standing in the middle, it feels high enough.

The bridge was built in the early 2000s to shorten the journey between the two sides of the gorge, linking the Dentam side with Uttarey. Before it, villagers faced a long walk or drive down to the stream and back up. Vehicles still use it, and it carries the shared jeeps between Gyalshing and Uttarey.

For visitors it is a stop rather than a destination. Park at one end, walk across and back, look down into the gorge and at the waterfalls on its walls, and continue to Uttarey or return to Pelling. It is part of most day trips west of Pelling and sits naturally between Dentam and a night in Uttarey.

story.title: Why a bridge this high was built
story.text: West Sikkim's hills are cut by deep gorges, and for most of their history the only way across was down to the river and up the other side on foot. Wikipedia's article on the Singshore Bridge, drawing on the Incredible India site and press coverage, says the bridge was built in the early 2000s, of iron and concrete, to shorten the distance between the two sides of the gorge and connect Dentam with Uttarey. The result is a span of about 240 m, more than 100 m above the stream, which is why it is now known as the highest bridge in Sikkim. For the villages beyond, including Uttarey near the Nepal border, it turned a long journey into a short drive and put them on the map for travellers. We do not know of any written record naming its engineers or giving an exact opening date, and the claim that it is the second highest bridge in Asia, repeated by the district administration and the press, is hard to check. What is certain is the effect: on a clear day, families from across Sikkim stop here for photographs, and the gorge below still carries the sound of the stream.
story.source: Wikipedia: Singshore Bridge, Pelling; Gyalshing district administration: Utteray

little_known.fact: Wikipedia gives the Singshore Bridge's length as 240 m (787 ft) and its height as more than 100 m (328 ft), and says it was built of iron and concrete.
According to Wikipedia, citing Incredible India, the Alpine Cheese Factory, which makes Gouda cheese, is located not far from the bridge.
The Gyalshing district administration's own page on Uttarey spells the bridge 'Singsor' and calls it 'said to be the second highest bridge in Asia'.

facts: Highest bridge in Sikkim, gorge views, waterfalls
Not needed for Indians; foreigners need the Sikkim RAP

highlights.title: Walk the 240 m span
highlights.text: Park at one end and walk across the bridge and back, about 15–20 minutes at an easy pace with stops. The deck is wide enough for vehicles, so stay on the edges and watch for jeeps. The middle of the span gives the best view straight down into the gorge.

highlights.title: Looking into the gorge
highlights.text: More than 100 m below, a stream runs through thick forest, and in the wetter months thin waterfalls streak the gorge walls. Morning light is softer and clearer; by afternoon cloud often fills the valley, which can be atmospheric in its own way.

highlights.title: The road from Dentam
highlights.text: The approach from Dentam climbs out of the farming valley through forest, with views back over terraces and villages. Stop on the bends above the bridge for a photograph of the whole span against the far side of the gorge.

highlights.title: On to Uttarey
highlights.text: Beyond the bridge the road climbs into oak, magnolia and rhododendron forest to Uttarey, at about 2,000 m. Lunch in a Uttarey homestay, a walk to the village monastery and a night there turn a quick stop into a relaxed day.

highlights.title: A good stop for families
highlights.text: There is no hike, no fee to speak of and no altitude to worry about, so the bridge suits grandparents and children alike. Hold children's hands on the deck, as railings are not designed for climbing, and keep clear of passing vehicles.

how_to_reach.text: Shared jeeps between Gyalshing and Uttarey cross the bridge, mostly in the morning, indicatively ₹150–250 a seat. Ask the driver to drop you at the bridge, but the next jeep may be hours away, so this suits travellers staying in Uttarey or Dentam.

From Pelling, about 26 km and 1–1.5 hours via Dentam. A half-day car to Dentam and the bridge costs indicatively ₹2,000–3,000; a full day on to Uttarey ₹3,000–4,000. From Gangtok, about 140 km and 6.5–7.5 hours via Legship and Gyalshing.

About 160–170 km and 7–8 hours via Melli, Jorethang, Legship, Gyalshing and Dentam. Almost everyone spends the first night in Pelling or goes straight to Uttarey. NH10 closes after heavy rain; the alternative road is via Darjeeling. Check current status before you travel.

costs: Free or a small fee; check current status
where_to_stay: There is nowhere to stay at the bridge itself. The closest beds are the family homestays of Uttarey, a short drive up the road beyond the bridge, at indicatively ₹1,200–2,200 per person with meals; we book them as Uttarey village homestays. Dentam, below, has a few basic homestays and lodges. Most travellers see the bridge on a day trip from Pelling, where Hotel Garuda is a budget base, Norbu Ghang Retreat and Spa a comfort option and The Elgin Mount Pandim the premium choice.
tips: Go in the morning, when the gorge is clearest and the road is quieter.
Walk on the edges of the deck and step aside for vehicles; it is a working road bridge.
Do not lean over or climb the railings, and hold small children's hands throughout.
Combine the bridge with Dentam and Uttarey; it is too far from Pelling for the bridge alone.
Avoid the road in heavy rain and after dark, when slides and poor visibility are risks.

experiences.title: Walk across Sikkim's highest bridge
experiences.best_time: Year-round, morning; best Oct–Dec and Mar–May
experiences.summary: Walk the full 240 m of the Singshore Bridge and back, stopping mid-span to look more than 100 m down into the forested gorge, on the road between Dentam and Uttarey.
body: The walk itself is simple: park at the Dentam end, walk to the far side and back, and stop as often as you like. Wikipedia gives the span as about 240 m and the height as more than 100 m, which makes it the highest bridge in Sikkim. At an easy pace the walk takes 15–20 minutes, and most people spend half an hour or more.

The view is best from the middle, looking straight down at the stream and along the gorge, where thin waterfalls run down the walls after rain. If you are nervous of heights, keep to the centre line when no vehicles are coming and look ahead rather than down.
This is a working road bridge, so watch for jeeps and cars, stay on the edges when they pass and do not stop vehicles for photographs.

faqs.q: How long and high is Singshore Bridge?
faqs.a: Wikipedia gives the length as about 240 m (787 ft) and the height as more than 100 m (328 ft) above the gorge, making it the highest bridge in Sikkim. It is often described as the second highest bridge in Asia, a claim repeated by the district administration that we have not been able to verify.

faqs.q: Is there an entry fee for Singshore Bridge?
faqs.a: The bridge is a public road, and walking across has generally been free; at times a small fee or parking charge may be collected. Check current status before you travel. There are few facilities, so carry water and use toilets in Dentam or Pelling before you come.

faqs.q: Is Singshore Bridge safe to walk on?
faqs.a: Yes, for normal walking. It is a steel and concrete road bridge that carries vehicles. Stay on the edges when traffic passes, do not lean over or climb the railings, hold children's hands and avoid crossing in very strong wind or heavy rain. People with a strong fear of heights may prefer to view it from the end.

experiences.title: Photograph the bridge and gorge
experiences.summary: Photograph the Singshore Bridge from the road bends above it and from mid-span, with the forested gorge, waterfalls and the far ridges, using soft morning light before cloud fills the valley.
body: The classic picture of the bridge is taken from the road above the Dentam end, where the whole span stretches across the gorge with forest on both walls. Ask your driver to stop on a safe bend with space to park, and use a moderate wide angle to keep the bridge and both sides in frame.

From the deck, look down for the stream and along the gorge for the thin waterfalls that appear in and just after the monsoon, in September and early October. In clear months, October to March, the morning light is clean and the far ridges stand out; afternoons often bring cloud rising from the valley.
Do not fly drones without the permissions now required in Sikkim, keep tripods out of the roadway and step aside for traffic. Ask before photographing local people crossing the bridge.

faqs.q: What is the best time to photograph Singshore Bridge?
faqs.a: Early to mid-morning from October to March, when the light is soft and the air clear. September and early October add waterfalls on the gorge walls, with more cloud. By afternoon cloud often rises from the valley, which can make moody pictures but hides the far side of the gorge.

faqs.q: Can I fly a drone at Singshore Bridge?
faqs.a: Drone flying in Sikkim needs permissions under Indian drone rules and often from local authorities, and the area is not far from the international border. Unless you have arranged permission in advance, do not fly. Rules change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Where is the best viewpoint for the whole bridge?
faqs.a: The road bends above the Dentam end give the clearest view of the full span with the gorge behind. Your driver will know where it is safe to stop. From the Uttarey side the view is partly blocked by trees. For close detail, walk to the middle of the deck.

experiences.title: Day drive: Dentam, Singshore and Uttarey
experiences.summary: A full day from Pelling down into the farming valley of Dentam, across the Singshore Bridge and up to the forest village of Uttarey near the Nepal border, with tea, a walk and a homestay lunch on the way.
body: Leave Pelling by 8–9 am. The road winds down for about an hour into Dentam's open valley of terraces and dairy farms; stop in the bazaar for milk tea. A few kilometres on, the road reaches the Singshore Bridge. Walk across, take your photographs and continue up through oak and rhododendron forest to Uttarey, at about 2,000 m.

In Uttarey, arrange lunch at a homestay through us or your driver, then walk up to the village's Kagyu monastery or along the first stretch of the forest trail. Start back by about 2 pm to reach Pelling before dark.
The circuit is around 70 km of narrow hill road. A night in Uttarey turns it into a far more relaxed trip, with time for the Mainbus waterfall walk the next morning.

faqs.q: Can I see Singshore Bridge and Uttarey in a day from Pelling?
faqs.a: Yes. It is about 70 km of hill road in total, so a full day with an early start. Leave by 8–9 am, stop in Dentam and at the bridge, have lunch in Uttarey and start back by 2 pm. A private car costs indicatively ₹3,000–4,000 for the day.

faqs.q: Is the road to Singshore Bridge and Uttarey good?
faqs.a: It is a narrow, winding hill road, paved for most of its length but with rough patches, especially after the monsoon. Local drivers handle it well. Slides can block it in June to September, and it is best avoided after dark. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Where can I eat on the Dentam–Uttarey drive?
faqs.a: Dentam bazaar has tea shops and small eateries for momos, noodles and thalis. Uttarey has no restaurants, but homestays will cook lunch with notice, indicatively ₹200–350 per person. Carry water and snacks, and tell us the day before so we can book a homestay lunch.

experiences.title: Birding on the forest road above the gorge
experiences.summary: Walk a quiet stretch of road from the Singshore Bridge up towards Uttarey in the early morning, when mixed flocks move through the forest above the gorge, with binoculars and, ideally, a local guide.
body: The forest on the slopes above the gorge, between the bridge and Uttarey, changes from warm broadleaf forest to oak, magnolia and rhododendron as the road climbs. Walking a stretch of the road in the early morning is an easy way to see birds without leaving the tarmac.

Stay in Uttarey or Dentam the night before so you can start at first light, when traffic is minimal. Watch for mixed flocks of minivets, warblers, tits and laughingthrushes, and for barbets calling from the canopy. Raptors sometimes soar over the gorge as the air warms.

Keep well to the side of the road, wear something visible and step off for vehicles. A local guide helps with identification and with finding side paths into the forest. Do not use playback to call birds.

faqs.q: Is Singshore Bridge good for birdwatching?
faqs.a: The bridge itself is a road crossing, but the forest on the road between the bridge and Uttarey is good for foothill and mid-altitude birds, especially in the early morning in spring and autumn. Stay overnight in Uttarey or Dentam to start at first light, before traffic picks up.

faqs.q: What birds can I see near Singshore and Uttarey?
faqs.a: Commonly seen birds of these forests include minivets, laughingthrushes, barbets, bulbuls, sunbirds, warblers and tits, with raptors over the gorge on warm days. Sightings vary with season and weather. A local guide and a field guide to Indian birds will help you identify what you see.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for birding near Singshore Bridge?
faqs.a: No permit is needed for Indian citizens walking the public road and village paths. Foreign nationals need Sikkim's Restricted Area Permit. Entering protected areas such as the Varsey sanctuary or walking towards the border needs separate permits. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Where is Singshore Bridge?
faqs.a: Singshore Bridge is in Gyalshing district (West Sikkim), on the road between Dentam and Uttarey, about 26 km and 1–1.5 hours by car west of Pelling. It spans a deep forested gorge. Although it is often called 'Singshore Bridge, Pelling', it is well beyond Pelling town.

faqs.q: How far is Singshore Bridge from Pelling?
faqs.a: About 26 km by road, roughly 1–1.5 hours each way via Dentam. A half-day private car from Pelling to Dentam and the bridge costs indicatively ₹2,000–3,000, and a full day continuing to Uttarey ₹3,000–4,000. Shared jeeps to Uttarey also cross the bridge.

faqs.q: Is Singshore Bridge the highest bridge in Asia?
faqs.a: No. Wikipedia calls it the highest bridge in Sikkim, at more than 100 m above the gorge, and it is widely described as the second highest bridge in Asia, a claim repeated by the district administration. Several much higher bridges exist in Asia today, so treat the ranking as a local saying.

faqs.q: How much time do I need at Singshore Bridge?
faqs.a: Thirty minutes to an hour is enough to walk across and back, take photographs and look into the gorge. Add an hour or so for the drive from Dentam and on to Uttarey. Most travellers combine the bridge with Dentam and Uttarey in a full day from Pelling.

faqs.q: Can vehicles drive across Singshore Bridge?
faqs.a: Yes. It is a road bridge, used by cars, taxis and shared jeeps between Dentam and Uttarey. Pedestrians share the deck, so walk on the edges and step aside when vehicles pass. Heavy vehicles may be restricted; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Singshore Bridge open in the monsoon?
faqs.a: The bridge itself stays open, but the roads to it from Pelling and Dentam can be blocked by landslides from June to September, and cloud often fills the gorge. If you visit in the monsoon, keep a flexible day and ask your driver about road conditions. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Are there facilities at Singshore Bridge?
faqs.a: Very few. There may be a small tea stall or vendor in season, and parking at the ends, but do not count on toilets or food. Use facilities and buy snacks in Pelling or Dentam, carry water and take your rubbish with you.

faqs.q: Who built Singshore Bridge and when?
faqs.a: Wikipedia says it was built in the early 2000s, of iron and concrete, to shorten the journey across the gorge between the Dentam and Uttarey sides. We have not found a published record of the exact opening date or the engineers responsible, so we leave those details out.

faqs.q: Is Singshore Bridge suitable for elderly travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. The bridge is reached by car and walking across is flat and short, about 15–20 minutes at an easy pace. The main concerns are traffic on the deck and the long drive from Pelling on winding roads. Travellers who get car-sick should take precautions and sit in front.
